history.summary: Major Shiva pilgrimage temple at Basukinath town, Jarmundi block, Dumka district, on the Deoghar-Dumka highway (24 km from Dumka, 42 km from Deoghar). Considered the 'court' (faujdari darbar) of Baba Bholenaath, where devotees seek justice. Shiva and Parvati temples face each other; legend holds the deities meet when both doors open in the evening. Complex holds 30+ shrines including a pond (Van Ganga / Shivaganga) for ritual bathing before darshan. A major stop for Kanwariyas carrying Ganga water from Sultanganj. CSV state error: CSV column holds town 'Dumka'; actual state is Jharkhand; actual town is Basukinath (Dumka district). Coordinates are town-level approximations - verify POI.

name: Basukinath Temple
town_description: Basukinath is a temple town in Jarmundi block of Dumka district, Jharkhand, on the Deoghar-Dumka highway, 24 km northwest of Dumka. It has its own railway station (2 km from the temple) and is a year-round pilgrimage stop for Baidyanath-bound devotees, swelling massively during Shravan. Basic hotels, dharamshalas and eateries serve pilgrims.

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport, about 52 km (taxis ~1 hour); Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi, about 250-280 km (sources differ).
travel.railway: Basukinath railway station, about 2 km from the temple; Jasidih Junction, about 50 km.
travel.road: On the Deoghar-Dumka highway (NH-114A); buses and taxis from Dumka (24 km, ~30 min) and Deoghar (42 km, ~1 hour).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan (July-August) for the Kanwariya season if prepared for crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: commonly 3:00 AM-4:00 PM and 6:00 PM-8:00 PM; another reports 4:00 AM-3:30 PM and 6:00-9:00 PM with a 12:00-2:00 PM bhog closure - verify locally. Extended hours during Shravan and Mahashivratri.
